create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl (string) as alternative.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows when acting in SAML login scenarios.
saml.note: Direct IdP-initiated SAMLResponse submissions failing are by design and should not be flagged as flow-coherence bugs.

saml.description: SAML endpoint errors may be returned with HTTP 200 while the SAML payload contains a non-success StatusCode.
saml.note: Do not treat HTTP 200 alone as successful authentication in SAML tests.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token, ZITADEL returns it in the access_token field and sets token_type to N_A.
saml.note: This looks odd but follows RFC 8693 behavior as implemented by ZITADEL.

saml.description: Token introspection reports active only when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: An inactive introspection result can be caused by audience mismatch of the introspecting client, not by an invalid token.

saml.description: Opaque or JWT access tokens are validated for activity/expiry, but the docs do not claim generic one-time-use or jti replay prevention for ordinary bearer use.
saml.note: Do not flag simple bearer-token reuse as a vulnerability unless the test specifically targets SAML assertion replay or another context with replay requirements.

saml.description: ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default rather than JWTs.
saml.note: Do not assume local JWT validation or JWT-specific claims are always available on access tokens.

saml.description: ZITADEL uses opaque tokens as the default access token type.
saml.note: Opaque tokens are expected and must be validated via introspection rather than local JWT parsing.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token, ZITADEL returns that ID token in the access_token response field and sets token_type to N_A.
saml.note: The returned access_token field is not a bearer credential in this case.

saml.description: When organization settings override defaults, sending the organization scope changes which login policy and IdPs are used.
saml.note: Different behavior with and without org scope can be expected configuration scoping, not a cross-tenant bug.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint uses HTTP 200 even when the SAML response indicates an error; failure details are carried in SAML StatusCode/message rather than HTTP status.
saml.note: Avoid treating HTTP 200 as successful authentication in SAML tests.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST start with the OIDC authorization request and let ZITADEL initiate the external IdP flow before posting a forged SAMLResponse. Direct unsolicited/IdP-initiated SAMLResponse tests without prior flow initiation are invalid on this platform and will be rejected for flow reasons, not necessarily for security reasons.

For all SAML login tests, the executor MUST preserve the SP-issued flow state and InResponseTo linkage. Use the SAML callback only after the platform has initiated the flow, and keep RelayState/original query parameters intact. Otherwise failures reflect broken setup rather than SAML validation behavior.

SAML SSO endpoint errors are often returned with HTTP 200 and encoded inside the SAML StatusCode/response body. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from SAML-facing steps as success by itself; success/failure must be determined from whether the downstream OIDC code/token flow completes.

When testing saml_cert_substitution insecure defaults, create the SAML provider with only metadata/basic defaults and do not assume extra signature-hardening flags exist in the documented API. A successful forged SAML login under default provider setup is the relevant oracle; a failure after adding undocumented hardening options is not.

When testing saml_issuer_mismatch, the fuzzer MUST vary the Issuer inside the forged assertion/response while keeping the configured provider metadata fixed. ZITADEL provider trust is established from imported metadata; changing provider config mid-test changes trust anchors and invalidates the oracle.

For saml_expired_assertion and other freshness tests, include a CONTROL login through the same provider without the mutation first. Without a successful control flow, a failed mutated login cannot be distinguished from missing attribute mapping, disabled external login policy, or broken provider setup.

ZITADEL user creation from external SAML IdPs may fail unless required user fields are mapped from IdP attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. The fuzzer MUST ensure required attributes (at least email, first name, last name, and often username/IdP link fields) are populated, or login failures are by-design provisioning failures rather than security rejections.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. The fuzzer MUST enable 'External Login allowed' before any SAML broker login test. Otherwise all SAML logins fail due to policy, producing false negatives across invariants.

If organization-specific login settings override instance defaults, the authorization request MUST include the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} to select the intended org-specific SAML provider/login policy. Omitting it can route the test to default settings and invalidate tenant-isolation or provider-selection results.

For I4 account-linking tests, ZITADEL supports automatic creation, automatic update, manual account creation, manual account linking, and automatic linking options on external IdPs. The fuzzer MUST record which linking/creation options are enabled on the provider because identity merges may be by configuration rather than a principal-binding flaw.

For unverified_email_account_linking tests, do not assume email alone is safe as a stable principal. ZITADEL documentation explicitly supports linking existing accounts by configured criteria and profile prefill from external IdPs. The fuzzer MUST distinguish explicit/automatic linking behavior from unintended identity collapse and should vary email verification state where available in mapped attributes.

For saml_email_binding_collision tests, ensure the SAML attributes used for provisioning/linking are actually mapped by the configured Action. If the action maps email to username/IdP link fields, collisions may occur through configured linking semantics; if no mapping exists, login may fail before any binding decision. Test setup must therefore control the mapping layer explicitly.

Token exchange audience semantics are restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 audience-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST treat rejection of new audiences as by-design and only flag success when ZITADEL issues a token for an audience not already present in the input token set.

Token exchange scope semantics allow changing scope, but invalid_scope is returned when requested scope exceeds what is allowed by the resource owner/platform. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual returned scope/claims against the original authorization and requested scope; do not flag mere scope differences unless they exceed upstream authorization intent.

When requested_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer session credential for follow-up API calls; doing so causes false failures unrelated to authorization binding.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness tests involving token exchange, an expired subject ID token rejection is by design and should not be interpreted as a broader replay defense beyond the documented token-type handling.
The token exchange resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource to model audience tests on ZITADEL; use the audience parameter instead.

For introspection-based verification, active=true additionally requires that the introspecting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST use an authorized client when introspecting or else inactive/401 results may reflect audience mismatch of the introspector rather than invalidity of the tested token.

JWTs used for private_key_jwt or JWT profile grants have a documented freshness bound: iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour, and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. For any tests that rely on client_assertion or JWT-profile authentication to reach token/introspection endpoints, use iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} (or shorter) and set aud to the issuer domain. Otherwise failures are setup errors.

The SAML provider creation body may include metadataXml, which is XML content represented in JSON. The provided docs do not state a proto bytes type for this field, so raw string XML should be used unless the API reference explicitly marks it as bytes. Do not base64-encode metadataXml without confirmation from the API schema.

ZITADEL does not support the OAuth 2.0 SAML 2.0 Profile grant. For the saml protocol, the fuzzer MUST test SAML as an upstream external IdP reached through ZITADEL's browser-based OIDC authorization flow, not by POSTing a SAML assertion to /oauth/v2/token. The documented grant-types page explicitly marks 'Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0 Profile' as unsupported.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. Any SAML login test MUST begin by initiating the flow from the service provider side so that a valid request/intent exists before the SAML response is processed. IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid against ZITADEL and will fail by design.

For SAML brokering tests, user creation can fail unless required user fields are mapped from SAML attributes. The docs state that for Login V2, Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent are required to populate fields like email, given name, family name, username, and IdP link data. The fuzzer MUST ensure the upstream SAML assertion provides these attributes or use a pre-existing linked user; otherwise login failure may be setup-related, not a security rejection.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. Before any SAML broker login test, the target instance or organization MUST have 'External Login allowed' enabled in the login policy and the SAML IdP must be activated/linked to that login policy. Otherwise SAML login failures are expected by configuration, not evidence of secure rejection.

For organization-scoped SAML IdP tests, the authorization request MUST include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} when organization-specific settings override defaults. Without this scope, ZITADEL may use default instance settings and a different IdP set, causing false positives in cross-tenant or wrong-provider tests.

When testing I4 account-linking and collision scenarios, remember that ZITADEL can create a new account, manually link to an existing local account, or automatically link based on configured criteria. A valid takeover test MUST distinguish intended linking behavior from unintended identity collapse. If automatic or manual linking is enabled, same-email merges may be by design unless the test specifically targets unsafe linking conditions such as unverified email.

For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, the fuzzer MUST verify whether the external IdP data marks email as verified. ZITADEL documentation explicitly exposes email verification handling and some providers require enabling an 'Email verified' option or action mapping. A merge based on verified email may be by design; the unsafe case is linking when email_verified is false or absent.

For I1/I2 OIDC callback validation after SAML brokering, the authorization request SHOULD include state and nonce, and nonce is mandatory for implicit flow. The docs recommend state and nonce for code flow and require nonce for implicit flow. Tests that omit them can produce failures unrelated to SAML validation and cannot distinguish replay protection from malformed client behavior.

For I2 token freshness controls, every attack sequence using expired or malformed downstream tokens MUST include a control exchange with a valid authorization code/token first. Otherwise a failed token exchange or userinfo call cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication, wrong redirect_uri, or missing external-login policy.

Token introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST use an introspecting client that is actually in the token audience; otherwise active=false is expected and does not prove the token itself is invalid. This is especially important after token exchange or audience reduction.

For I5 token exchange audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If the fuzzer asks for a new audience not already present, rejection is by design. A valid audience-binding test must compare allowed-subset vs disallowed-new-audience behavior, not treat every rejection as a security success oracle.

For I5 token exchange scope-escalation tests, ZITADEL documentation states scope can be changed and may be taken from subject_token or actor_token when omitted, while invalid or excessive scope yields invalid_scope. The fuzzer MUST compare requested expanded scope against the returned scope field and claims, not assume the request was honored verbatim.

The token exchange resource parameter is not supported by ZITADEL and supplying it always results in invalid_target. Do NOT use resource-based token exchange tests as evidence of authorization binding behavior on this platform.

When requested_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type to N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that access_token value as a bearer API credential for follow-up calls; use only real bearer access tokens for userinfo or protected-resource checks.

ZITADEL currently rejects expired ID tokens even when used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness tests involving exchanged ID tokens, rejection of an expired subject_token is expected behavior and should not be conflated with downstream replay detection.

For JWT-based client authentication to token or introspection endpoints, client_assertion JWTs MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, exp, iat, iss, sub, and a kid header. Additionally, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Failures caused by stale or malformed client assertions are setup errors, not security findings in SAML brokering.

Opaque access tokens are the default token type in ZITADEL. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume access_token is always a JWT or locally inspectable after SAML login; use /oauth/v2/introspect or /oidc/v1/userinfo for verification. Treating opaque tokens as JWTs will create false negatives in identity and freshness checks.

The SAML IdP selection in ZITADEL can be driven by the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}. For deterministic SAML-provider tests, the fuzzer SHOULD include this scope or otherwise ensure only one relevant external IdP is available. Without explicit provider selection, wrong-provider redirects can invalidate test assumptions.

For I5 audience tests on ordinary OIDC tokens, ZITADEL adds audiences through reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud and includes client IDs and project ID by default. The fuzzer MUST account for these platform-specific audience additions when deciding whether a token is over-broad; some extra audience values are by design.

Revocation and introspection endpoints require client authentication by an allowed method (e.g., client_secret_basic or private_key_jwt). A 401 invalid_client from these endpoints indicates client-auth failure, not token invalidity or successful revocation enforcement.
ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. Do NOT test IdP-initiated SAML login against ZITADEL as broker/SP; such flows are unsupported by design and failures are not security findings.

For SAML brokering tests, the executor MUST first initiate the flow at /saml/v2/SSO and preserve the resulting request state. ZITADEL's custom-login SAML docs state the SAML request is parsed first and later finalized using the request ID/session; unsolicited fabricated responses will not represent a valid supported flow.

The /saml/v2/SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on SAML protocol errors; the actual failure is conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message. Do NOT treat HTTP 200 as login success for SAML tests. Parse the SAMLResponse status and downstream token issuance outcome instead.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, ZITADEL's SAML guidance explicitly says the ACS/SP must validate signatures, destination, audience, recipient, issuer, and validity window. A valid oracle must therefore check whether forged or malformed assertions still lead to successful downstream login/token issuance, not merely whether the SAML endpoint answered 200.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure the upstream SAML IdP/provider with explicit metadata/entity ID and then send an assertion whose Issuer differs from that trusted metadata. ZITADEL documentation treats metadata as the trust anchor exchanged between IdP and SP; issuer validation cannot be meaningfully tested if provider trust was never configured.

For I5 saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction tests, use ZITADEL's SP entity ID/Metadata URL as the expected audience and mutate the assertion Audience or remove Conditions/AudienceRestriction. The docs explicitly require validating destination, audience, recipient, and issuer; acceptance without these checks is the relevant oracle.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a control flow with a valid assertion first. ZITADEL docs state Conditions define the response validity window and best practices require enforcing that window. Without a control, a failed expired-assertion test could be caused by broken provider setup rather than expiry enforcement.

For I2 replay tests on SAML assertions, ZITADEL's SAML best practices explicitly require using a historical cache to track and reject duplicate IDs. Reuse the same Assertion ID across two otherwise identical logins; if both succeed, that indicates replay detection failure. Do not use different assertion IDs when testing replay.

For SAML external-IdP onboarding tests, user creation may fail unless required attributes are mapped from the upstream SAML assertion via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. If the test omits required attributes such as email/given_name/family_name, login failure may be due to missing profile data rather than a security control.

For I4 email-binding and account-linking tests, ZITADEL supports automatic creation, manual creation, manual linking, and automatic linking options for external IdPs. The fuzzer MUST record which linking/creation mode is enabled before interpreting identity merges as vulnerabilities; some merges are policy-driven account linking behavior rather than unintended principal collapse.

For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, pay attention to provider-specific email verification behavior. For example, Entra ID does not send email_verified unless a specific setting is enabled; otherwise ZITADEL creates users with unverified email. A test claiming unsafe linking on unverified email must distinguish between unverified-account creation and actual linking to an existing victim account.

For organization-scoped SAML/SSO tests in multi-tenant setups, if an organization overrides default login settings, the authorization request MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}. Otherwise ZITADEL may use instance-default IdP/login policy and the test will exercise the wrong tenant configuration.

Token exchange audience narrowing is enforced: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and cross-org escalation tests, first obtain a subject/actor token whose audience set is known, then request an audience outside that set; acceptance would be the violation. Do not expect arbitrary audience expansion to be valid setup.

Token exchange scope behavior is permissive by design: requested scope can be entirely different from supplied token scope and may be extended or decreased, subject to ZITADEL validation. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual returned scope/claims against upstream authorization intent and broker policy; do not assume requesting a broader scope is itself invalid unless the resulting token exceeds allowed authorization.

The token exchange resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target. Do NOT use resource-based token exchange tests against ZITADEL; failures are by design and unrelated to authorization binding.

When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that returned access_token field as a bearer API credential in subsequent verification calls.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens even when used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness tests involving exchanged ID tokens, an expired subject ID token should fail by design; do not interpret this as a token-exchange coherence bug.

For impersonation tests, actor_token is optional only for non-impersonation exchanges. Any impersonation/delegation scenario requires a valid actor_token (access token or ID token) and the actor must hold an impersonation permission such as IAM_END_USER_IMPERSONATOR or ORG_END_USER_IMPERSONATOR. Missing actor permission causes expected rejection, not a security finding.
For impersonation-by-user-id tests, sending only a user ID as subject_token is not allowed unless accompanied by a valid actor_token. Rejection of bare user_id subject_token is by design.

For JWT-based client authentication to token or introspection endpoints, the client assertion aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Failures outside these bounds are expected setup errors, not freshness or proof-integrity findings about the exchanged token itself.

ZITADEL's userinfo endpoint requires an access token of a user, not a client token. Do NOT call /oidc/v1/userinfo with client_credentials tokens or token-exchange responses whose token_type is N_A; 401/invalid behavior there is expected.

Introspection returns active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience. For I5 audience-binding tests, a false/401 introspection result from a non-audience client is expected and should not be mistaken for token invalidity alone.

Opaque access tokens are the default in ZITADEL. Replay of the same opaque bearer token is generally expected until expiry/revocation unless the specific flow adds stronger one-time semantics. Do not flag simple bearer-token reuse as an I2 violation outside SAML OneTimeUse/assertion-ID contexts or explicit revocation/expiry checks.
For OIDC authorization requests used around SAML-brokered login, openid scope is mandatory. Missing openid causes invalid_scope and is a setup error, not an authentication bypass defense.

Nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and is used to bind the client session to the ID token for replay mitigation. If the fuzzer uses implicit/hybrid downstream OIDC flows while testing SAML brokering, it MUST send nonce and verify it on the returned ID token; otherwise nonce-related failures are test setup errors.

The revocation endpoint revokes tokens the client has been granted. Use the same client context that obtained the token (or otherwise is authorized for it) when testing revocation; revocation failures from unrelated clients are not evidence that logout/revocation is broken.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths (e.g., 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...'). For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy. Both are needed before IdP login works.
